A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The earlier SVD appendix and task lists can be matched to Appendix D and Tables 7–8 in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original forgetting measurements, low-rank analyses, prediction errors, and replay experiments in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds online/SVD replay experiments, downstream task evaluations, and component-level analyses.

M1.justification: v2 uses two fine-tuning passes and leaves online prediction to future work. Section 4.2 of v3 adds an online variant that replays random examples for the first 10% of training, evaluates seed forgetting, then uses predicted forgetting for the remaining 90%. This eliminates the preliminary full training pass; SVD predictions also become available for replay.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds downstream benchmark evaluation after Dolly fine-tuning, including previously unreported SciQ, Winogrande, MMLU-Pro, IFEval, MUSR, and GPQA evaluations. This substantially broadens tested task coverage while retaining the original fine-tuning and upstream datasets.

E2.justification: Figure 6 adds SVD-based replay comparisons alongside KNN. SVD was already evaluated for prediction in v2, but was absent from its replay comparison. Random, PPL, MIR, Grad, and the ground-truth reference are retained; v2's KNN replay becomes Offline KNN.

E3.justification: Table 1 adds Pearson correlation, and Appendix C introduces task-specific accuracy metrics and zero-, three-, and five-shot evaluation settings. Online replay introduces a different training-pass budget and replay schedule. v3 also explicitly reports additional SVD hyperparameter tuning, although the revised settings are unspecified.

E4.justification: v3 adds a representation-similarity diagnostic and online/offline replay comparisons. Appendix D extends the retained SVD visualizations with an analysis of the top three tasks and top 50 upstream examples per component, identifying domain and task patterns in Table 6.

E5.justification: Appendix D introduces a z-test comparing component-specific domain frequencies with those among the overall top 50 forgotten examples. Single-run association statistics, ten seed-set repetitions for prediction, and paired t-tests for replay remain documented in both versions; no increased repeat count is reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 corrects correlation results following an implementation issue: TF-IDF Spearman correlation changes from 0.004 to -0.035, for example. Retuning replaces Table 2's SVD scores: in-domain OLMo-7B Full FT changes from 7.53 to 7.14, while out-of-domain OLMo-7B-Instruct Full FT changes from 39.03 to 40.47. SVD replaces KNN as the generally lowest-error predictor. Figure 6 and Tables 4–6 add replay, downstream, and component findings.

T1.justification: New Table 3 adds analytical cost accounting for replay methods, including offline cost 2FT(Y)+EV(S)+MC versus online cost FT(Y)+EV(S)+MC and repeated inference costs for MIR. The existing SVD, rank approximation, and Taylor-expansion mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same core claims: forgetting associations have low-rank structure, matrix completion predicts forgetting effectively, and prediction-guided replay reduces upstream log-perplexity degradation.

C2.justification: v3 substantially qualifies practical applicability: significant downstream task benefits are not established, and replay alone may be insufficient. It explains the online accuracy–cost tradeoff, interprets SVD components through domain/task patterns, and explicitly discusses unresolved effects of model scaling and other experimental factors.

D1.justification: v3 specifies TF-IDF cosine similarity, OLMo-1B final-layer representations, the online replay schedule, and LM-Evaluation-Harness for downstream testing. It removes the abstract's project-page URL. Additional SVD tuning is acknowledged, but Appendix B's detailed parameter description remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gao et al. (2024) for the evaluation framework. The related-work section and positioning relative to forgetting prediction, data attribution, and continual learning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Targeted edits refine the introduction and expand Section 4's replay and efficiency explanations. v3 adds a limitations paragraph and a downstream-evaluation Appendix C, moving the existing association appendix to D. Most prose and the main section order are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a representation row and Pearson column; Figure 6 expands to online/offline KNN and SVD bars with an added legend. New Tables 3–6 display costs, downstream performance, and component interpretations. Existing heatmaps are retained, and the original task-list Tables 3–4 become Tables 7–8.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses v2's explicit extra-training-pass limitation with an evaluated online method, corrects faulty correlation results, and tests whether perplexity benefits extend to downstream tasks. Reporting the lack of established significant downstream gains materially clarifies applicability. These changes substantially strengthen practical utility and evidential reliability, despite incomplete documentation of SVD retuning and removal of the project-page link.
